title: Work and Energy
scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT Physics, Mathematics and Research Reasoning lessons. Models and calculations use stated assumptions. Independent scientific review is pending; this is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Kinetic energy for nonrelativistic translation is ½mv². Gravitational potential near Earth can be written mgh relative to a chosen zero; elastic potential for an ideal spring is ½kx².

For a system with only conservative work exchanged internally, mechanical energy can remain constant while kinetic and potential forms trade. Total energy conservation is broader than mechanical-energy conservation.
Friction can convert organized mechanical energy into internal energy. Energy has not disappeared when mechanical energy decreases.
Define the system boundary and included forms before applying conservation. A change in the potential-energy reference shifts values without changing measurable energy differences.

steps.text: For a constant force, work on an object is W = Fd cos θ, where θ is between force and displacement. Work is a scalar that may be positive, negative or zero.
Net work equals the change in kinetic energy. A force perpendicular to displacement does no work, even if its magnitude is large.
Average power is work divided by time. Instantaneous mechanical power is the dot product F·v; force magnitude alone does not determine power.
Lifting a load at constant speed can require positive work by the lifter while gravity does equal negative work. Zero net work is compatible with nonzero work by individual forces.

steps.text: Mechanical advantage is output force divided by input force. An ideal lossless machine trades a smaller input force for a greater input displacement.
For an ideal machine, input work equals output work. Real machines have efficiency below one when some input energy is dissipated outside the desired output.
Count supporting rope segments for a specified ideal pulley arrangement; the number of visible pulleys alone does not determine mechanical advantage.
Efficiency is useful output energy divided by input energy. Force gain does not imply energy gain, and a force comparison alone does not establish efficiency.
